evidence.fitness: A researcher cannot build a predictor on this: the only signal is source line number on one generated file, with 11 distinct lines (line-level 1-NN LOLO agreement 10/11, Wilson 0.62-0.98; mutant-level 25/27 Wilson 0.77-0.98). No prior work is cited: equivalent-mutant detection by trivial compiler equivalence (Papadakis et al., ICSE 2015), predictive mutation testing (Zhang et al., ISSTA 2016), hardware mutation tools (YosysHQ MCY, Synopsys Certitude's non-activated/non-propagated classes), and solver-runtime prediction (SATzilla). Its value is as a pilot that later projects (eda-equivinterval, eda-conefeat, eda-conehash, eda-equivxfer) did build on; the result itself is not new or publishable.
evidence.domain: Generated the golden RTL (eda_harness Problem().verilog({'p':8,'wb':4})) and read the mutated lines. Line 151 `if ((grp + 1) * P < (layer ? 4 : 8))` is always false at P=8 (grp is never incremented), so all 8 line-151 survivors are dead-code mutants that constant propagation would remove; lines 140-145 are boundary-benign clamp/shift changes after `v<0` clamps (e.g. >>> -> >> on a non-negative v); line 123 mutants change reset values that IDLE/start overwrites, which are plausibly sequentially equivalent but defeat register-matched equiv_induct, so 'undecided' there measures a solver limitation rather than hardness of a cone. A referee would say the 'signal' is mutation semantics (dead code / benign boundary / reset-state change), that a TCE-style baseline (Yosys opt + netlist compare, ~1 s) is the obvious missing comparison, and that the CPU being saved is mostly the ~210 s of exhausted bounded SAT that eda-verify runs before induction (eda-earlystop README:30), so the 55% depends on phase order. None of this is in the README.

defects.what: The 'smoother rules do worse' comparison for the one-split rule is a tie-break artefact: cuts are training-line values with the lowest tied cut chosen, so under LOLO the stump scores 20/27; with midpoint cuts it scores 25/27 for 3,298 s, identical to 1-NN. Later projects (eda-conefeat, eda-conehash) adopt 'a one-split rule under leave-one-line-out, the score eda-equivpredict uses'.

Stated mechanism is wrong: README says the provable region is 'probably deep arithmetic cones'; in the generated RTL line 151 is a branch that is dead at P=8, lines 140-145 are benign clamp/shift boundary changes, and line 123 reset-value changes are plausibly sequentially equivalent but defeat register-matched equiv_induct. The 'signal' is mutation semantics, and 'undecided' is a solver limitation.

No prior work and no structural baseline: equivalent-mutant detection by trivial compiler equivalence (Papadakis et al., ICSE 2015), predictive mutation testing (Zhang et al., ISSTA 2016), MCY/Certitude not cited; a TCE-style Yosys opt + netlist compare would likely flag the 8 dead-code line-151 equivalents in about a second each and is the baseline a referee would ask for.
Core logic untested: 3 of 5 seeded mutations survive (kills_lost counts undecided instead of killed; stump cut comparison; kind tie rule); no test pins any headline number in results.txt.

The 55% saving is priced in eda-verify's phase order (about 210 s of exhausted bounded SAT before every proof, eda-earlystop README:30); running induction first would change the cost being predicted. Not stated.

verdict: Every number reproduces: my own script from the raw eda-verify log, without importing the subject, matches all twelve policy rows, the 7,414/3,746 CPU-s costs and the 93% (25/27) nearest-line accuracy, and run.py regenerates results.txt byte-identical. It does not meet the bar. The tests catch 2 of 5 seeded bugs. The comparison between predictors depends on how the one-split rule breaks ties: with midpoint cuts it equals 1-NN at 25/27, so 'smoother rules do worse' is not supported. The mechanism the README offers ('deep arithmetic cones') is contradicted by the generated RTL. Line 151 is dead code at P=8, lines 140-145 are benign boundary changes, and the line-123 'undecided' mutants are reset-value changes that register-matched induction cannot prove. So the signal is mutation semantics plus a solver limitation, and a trivial-compiler-equivalence baseline and the mutation-testing prior work are both missing. The README is honest about its limits (one design, 11 distinct lines, no interval). As research it is a pilot that later projects built on, not a result a DAC/ICCAD referee would accept.
